paper_id: Ji et al. - 2014 - Walking down the STAIRS Efficient collision resolution for wireless sensor networks
title: Walking down the STAIRS: Efficient collision resolution for wireless sensor networks
motivation: Collisions in duty-cycled WSNs waste energy and cause severe latency; existing backoff solutions degrade under bursty traffic.
problem_framing: Collision resolution as identifying N contenders efficiently in one round via RSSI stairs pattern, instead of sequential backoff.
key_insight: Constructive interference creates RSSI stair-step pattern; counting falling edges reveals number of simultaneous senders.
method_signature: Superimposed identical packets generate measurable RSSI stairs; assign channel slots by CP packet length.
evaluation_criteria: Latency reduction and throughput improvement vs Strawman and CSMA backoff; detection accuracy of falling edges.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: In sparse low-rate networks STAIRS advantages diminish; CSMA backoff shows efficiency in simplicity.
evidence_for_taste: at most one sender can be identified and win the channel access in each round
the performance may suffer serious degradation in duty cycled WSNs
this intentionally generated stair pattern of RSSI provides a helpful tool
external interference from 802.11 Wifi networks may generate some falling edges
the general detection accuracy is around 90% for all the 5 cases
thinking_moves: 从叠加信号异常反推物理层可利用特征
把perception问题(reidentifying contenders)重新frame成communication问题(channel assignment)
把碰撞场景建模为ball-and-bin分配问题
理论推导RSSI公式后做实证验证
识别工程挑战(同步精度+RSSI噪声)并分别攻克
